title: Take to Heart
text: “Meteor Bow!”

Itsuki fires this skill—which sends an arrow followed by a trail of stars and deals area-of-effect damage—at her Father. However, he takes the hit head-on and remains completely unfazed. Itsuki really needs to weaken him a bit here.
“Aiming Lancer!”
Right after the cooldown ended, he pierced through Itsuki and her companions with minimal firepower, without any buffs.
“Waaaaaah!”
Itsuki and his companions collapsed, groaning in pain. Now for the rest…
“Paralyze Lance!”
It’d be a hassle if they started thrashing around recklessly. So I drove the paralyzing lance right into Itsuki. He shouldn’t be able to move for a while now.

Come to think of it, the look on Itsuki’s face right before he was struck by the Paralyze Lance was quite a sight. It was as if he were saying, “This is just like an event battle, isn’t it?” Unfortunately, this is reality—so while there may be a winner and a loser, it’s certainly not a game event.
“Ugh…”
Éclair rode her horse over to where Trash was. The soldiers had already been swept aside.
“Now then, you impostor posing as the Wise King… By the Queen’s command, you are to be taken to our country.”
“Guh… I—I haven’t lost!”
“Indeed… it’s unthinkable that a wise and wise king would be captured so easily…”

The representative of the Shusaku clan is muttering as he stares at Eclair. Hmm? The Crimson Swine isn’t here? Just as I was thinking that, Trash—perhaps realizing he’s at a disadvantage—is trying to abandon both Itsuki and Kuzu and make a run for it. Where do you plan to run, I wonder?
“I won’t let you get away! Air Strike Javelin!”
I ran after him and pierced him from behind. Didn’t Éclair say it herself? That we were only to capture Trash. In other words, the Crimson Swine is no longer under our jurisdiction.
“Oink—!?”
Pierced by my spear, the Crimson Swine is making a racket.
“It’s time to settle the score.”
My father and Éclair are quietly watching the scene. After a while, Éclair muttered,
“Myne, the adventurer posing as the Princess of Melromarc. I’ve been entrusted with a message from the Queen. She says, ‘You’ve gone too far.’”
“Oink! Oink!”
It’s tougher than I expected. But this pig’s squeals are grating on my ears. I should finish it off quickly.
“Burst Lance X!”

“
Éclair seems to be thinking about something while looking at me… no, that’s not it. She’s staring at the spot where the Crimson Swine was. At her feet, Trash is reaching out toward us.
“Maltyiiiiiiiiii!”
Trash screamed. Another piece of trash has been wiped from this world. I feel a sense of relief, somehow.
“Sorry, but all this commotion is getting annoying. I’m outta here!”
With a thud, Éclair struck Trash hard on the back of the head, and Trash went limp—probably unconscious.
“‘Wooooooooo!’”
Cries of victory rang out from both the Siltvelt Army and the Melromarc Army that Éclair had brought along.
“The battle isn’t over yet, but I guess we can catch our breath for a bit… maybe?”
“Now we just need Shieldfreeden to give up.”
“That’s not going to happen. It won’t end until we take out those remaining Aotatsu.”
“True… I suppose. But since they’ve realized they’re at a disadvantage, I think we can buy ourselves a little time.”
“Yeah, fortunately, none of the nations have suffered enough losses to compromise their ability to fight the waves.”
“Come to think of it, why is the Melromarc army on our side?”
Father’s question is a valid one. As Éclair mentioned earlier, it’s likely because of the Queen of Melromarc.

“The Queen has always been opposed to war. Furthermore, I relayed to her the vision of the future that Lord Kitamura spoke of. That wasn’t the only factor, but after considering various elements, she decided on a course of action to ensure that the forces needed to fight the Waves aren’t lost.”
“I see. Siltvelt and Melromarc… if either one were to fall, it would make fighting the Wave much harder…”

“Indeed. Furthermore, with the death of Takt, the ‘Hero of the Whip,’ it was confirmed that multiple owners of Seven Star Weapons are now missing from Faubrey. In light of this, Faubrey has no intention of cooperating with Shieldfreeden and has decided to focus on investigating the cause.”
“I see. I hope this means we can put the war aside and finally fight the Waves with everything we’ve got.”

That’s right. We shot down every single one of the airplanes Takt was pushing for, and as you can see, even our trump card, Itsuki, is out of the picture. All that’s left is to prepare for the incoming Waves. Hmm?
“This isn’t what we agreed on!”

One of Itsuki’s comrades, who’s just recovered from the battle—the one in the fancy armor… the guy who got smoked in the future, if I recall correctly—has started making a fuss. This goes back to the coup d’état. I believe he was the ringleader back then, when we took control of the castle town alongside Filolial-sama and the others on Father’s orders. By the way, Smoked Meat—wasn’t he originally part of Ren’s group, chosen by the nation in the first world? I think he left after a few days and joined Itsuki’s party.
“Ugh… ah…”
Since Itsuki took a hit from my Paralyze Lance, he’s paralyzed and can’t move.
“What kind of champion of justice are you! You impostor masquerading as a champion of justice!”
“That’s right, that’s right!”

I’m sensing some kind of ominous vibe here. Itsuki’s too close for me to take him down immediately. Thinking it was just an internal squabble, my Father and the others were a split second too slow to react.
“You weak, fake Bow Hero! We’ll put an end to you!”

With that, the Smoked Meats brandished the weapons they’d dropped on the ground and brought them down on Itsuki, who was paralyzed and unable to move. Their movements were so fast that even I was caught off guard. After all, I’d moved a little way back to take down the Crimson Swine.

Even the Aiming Lancer wouldn’t be able to fire in time due to the aiming delay. Even if I fired a Brionac… Gungnir… or an Air Strike Javelin, Itsuki was too close—at best, I could silence one or two of them.
“Air Strike Javelin! Gungnir!”
“Itsuki! Air Strike—”
Reacting to my move, my father instinctively tried to cast a defensive skill.
“Guh!”
“M-my hand—”

I also used Skills to blow off the weapon-wielding hands of about two of them—a bit rough, I admit. However, the leader of the Smoked Meat crew—the one in the flashy armor—swinged his axe down at Itsuki, who was immobilized.
“Ah… ga—!!”
“Ha ha ha! We’ve defeated the fake Bow Hero! This seals our victory! O Shield Hero and Spear Hero! We’ve been deceived!”

Fresh blood gushed from what had been Itsuki, and the Smoked Meat was shouting at us in a mysterious, flavor-related tone. Judging by his expression, he must’ve thought he was on our side. How should we make this Smoked Meat pay for this?
“No way… Just when we finally had a glimmer of hope to end this war…”
“You bastards!”
Éclair rushed toward the Smoked Meat creature, ready to slash at it with her sword. But—
“…Motoyasu. It seems the conditions for the rewind have been met.”
Father announced this with an expression that suggested he had realized everything. That’s right—the time remaining was the very brief moment before Itsuki’s life ran out.
“I’m sorry. It’s all because Motoyasu’s power wasn’t enough…”
“…I really want to thank you so much, but since there’s no time, I’ll just say what’s on my mind.”
“Understood. Please say whatever you like.”
“First, I’m sorry for putting all this hardship on you alone. It looks like this is as far as I can go, but I’m rooting for you.”
“To hear such words from you, Father—it is a great honor for this Motoyasu.”
“Ahaha… Somehow, before I knew it, I’d gotten used to being called ‘Father.’ I really wanted to meet that girl, Filo, whom you like, Motoyasu…”
“…I see.”

“Now, seriously, Motoyasu, you have a rather radical side, so be careful with your actions. Under no circumstances should you entertain the idea that destroying a country or a religion will end conflict. You’d be better off abandoning that line of thinking. It’s bound to fail. No matter what organization it is, if you just take out the leader, the remnants will just run amok, just like with Takt. In fact, it’ll just end with a new leader taking his place.”
“I understand. I’ll keep that in mind.”
Eventually, my Father let out a complex smile—part wry, part resigned.

“I was so happy to have Motoyasu-kun help me in this world. Thank you. It was a short time, but I really enjoyed it. If we’re going to rewind, please make sure I don’t make the same mistake next time… I beg you—”
His voice trailed off mid-sentence.
A bow icon lit up in my field of vision. The world turned gray, and everything came to a standstill. Then… the spear trembled… a clock appeared, and the rewind began.
“I understand, Father. This Motoyasu—next time, just as you asked… I’ll do my best to prevent war from breaking out and use my knowledge of the future to my advantage.”

It seems that if I go to Siltvelt to protect my Father, it will lead to a war that engulfs the entire world. The same result would likely occur in Shieldfreeden, where Takt is. I need to think more carefully to prevent this from happening. That is my Father’s wish. So then… how can I create a world without war?

…Come to think of it, in the first world, while there were civil conflicts, wars hardly ever broke out. If I analyze what that meant and act accordingly, it will naturally lead to fulfilling Father’s wish.
Violence is power, but so is intellect. Based on the information I’ve gained through these loops, I will keep the promise I made to Father.
And so, I—returned to the past.
The Siltvelt arc has come to an end. Starting with the next episode, we’ll move on to the Melromarc arc.
